{{Short description|Chemistry academic and head of School of Chemistry at the University of Sydney}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Ruth Gall''' (born '''Ruth Edna Lack'''; 8 November 1923 – 10 July 2017<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2018-02-27|title=Lessons from an extraordinary woman|url=https://www.sydney.edu.au/study/why-choose-sydney/student-life/student-news/2018/02/27/lessons-from-an-extraordinary-woman.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200804235549/https://www.sydney.edu.au/study/why-choose-sydney/student-life/student-news/2018/02/27/lessons-from-an-extraordinary-woman.html|archive-date=2020-08-04|access-date=2021-10-12|website=The University of Sydney|language=en-AU}}</ref>) was an Australian chemist<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Allen|first=N|date=1994|title=Achievement in Science: The Careers of Two Australian Women Chemists.|url=http://www.publish.csiro.au/?paper=HR9941020129|journal=Historical Records of Australian Science|language=en|volume=10|issue=2|pages=129|doi=10.1071/HR9941020129|issn=0727-3061|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and Head of School at the [[University of Sydney School of Chemistry|School of Chemistry]], [[University of Sydney]]. She was the first female Head of School at the university.<ref name=":1" />

== Early life ==
Gall attended and won sporting<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article17261955 |title=MERIDAN SCHOOL SPORTS. |newspaper=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |issue=30,772 |location=New South Wales, Australia |date=18 August 1936 |accessdate=12 October 2021 |page=16 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref> and academic<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article17546367 |title=SCHOOL PRIZE LISTS. |newspaper=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |issue=31,503 |location=New South Wales, Australia |date=20 December 1938 |accessdate=12 October 2021 |page=18 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article17437831 |title=MERIDEN, STRATHFIELD. |newspaper=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |issue=31,186 |location=New South Wales, Australia |date=15 December 1937 |accessdate=12 October 2021 |page=24 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article17293727 |title=SPEECH DAYS. |newspaper=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |issue=30,874 |location=New South Wales, Australia |date=15 December 1936 |accessdate=12 October 2021 |page=18 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article17124391 |title=SCHOOL PRIZE DISTRIBUTION LISTS. |newspaper=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |issue=30,247 |location=New South Wales, Australia |date=12 December 1934 |accessdate=12 October 2021 |page=21 |via=National Library of Australia}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|date=14 December 1933|title=MERIDEN|page=10 (FINAL EXTRA)|newspaper=[[The Sun (Sydney)|The Sun]]|issue=7475|location=New South Wales, Australia|url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article230192715|via=National Library of Australia|accessdate=12 October 2021}}</ref> prizes at [[Meriden School]], a girls school where chemistry and physics were not taught at the time.<ref name=":0" />

Soon after she completed her schooling, [[World War II]] broke out. Gall enlisted in the Women's Auxiliary Air Force (WAAF) and was sent to work on radar operations in Northern Queensland.<ref name=":0" />

In 1944, at the age of 21 she returned to Sydney and was allowed under the [[Commonwealth Reconstruction Training Scheme]] to start university study in Science.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Gall took on some industrial positions, including working for British Industrial Solvents in London,<ref name=":0" /> where she shifted into a research role, before returning to Australia.<ref name=":1" /> After a short period in the Australian subsidiary of BIS, she secured a research role investigating coal at the CSIRO.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=The University of Melbourne eScholarship Research Centre|title=Gall, Ruth - Biographical entry - Encyclopedia of Australian Science|url=https://www.eoas.info/biogs/P004918b.htm|access-date=2021-10-12|website=www.eoas.info|language=en-gb}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

Gall was attracted through discussion with [[Sever Sternhell]] to further study, and a teaching fellowship in the Department of Organic Chemistry, part of the School of Chemistry at the University of Sydney.<ref name=":1" /> She completed her PhD under the supervision of [[Charles Shoppee]] in 1961.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

Gall's academic career was entirely at the School of Chemistry at the University of Sydney.<ref name=":1" /> Her research concentrated on the fundamental study of steroids, including mechanisms, synthesis, and NMR spectroscopy.<ref name=":1" /> She began as a lecturer in 1962.<ref name=":0" /> There was opposition to her appointment based on her gender, but this was soon overcome as she established good relationships with both students and colleagues.<ref name=":1" />

She was promoted to Senior Lecturer in 1966 and associate professor in 1969.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

She became Head of School with unanimous support immediately after a change of rules allowed Associate Professors to take up the role.<ref name=":1" />

== Honours, decorations, awards and distinctions ==
Gall has been honoured with a named lectureship, the Ruth Gall Memorial Lecture, on [[International Women's Day]],<ref name=":0" /> and a portrait painting of her by Kate Gradwell<ref>{{Cite web|title=2019 and before|url=https://www.kategradwell.com/news-1|access-date=2021-10-12|website=Kate Gradwell Art|language=en}}</ref> is on the wall of Chemistry Lecture Theatre 3, named in her honour as the Ruth Gall Lecture Theatre.<ref>{{Cite web|title=238 Lecture theatre 3 at USYD Camperdown/Darlington|url=https://studentvip.com.au/usyd/main/maps/142654|access-date=2021-10-12|website=StudentVIP|language=en}}</ref>
